non-AcceptSafe policy: a face-count threshold is not derivable from the datasheet. Rust-era; no legacy Python source. The derivable alternative fails outright -- gating on 'the mesh is finer than the printer can resolve' (surface_area / (pixel x layer)) puts a mini-sized model's resolvable face count near 1e6, so it would forbid decimating the 429,120-face Weeping Treant as well. The honest statement is that downstream cost is superlinear in face count while the geometric price is bounded by the Derived deviation limits, which makes this a corpus-shaped policy gate. It decides only whether to attempt, never whether a result is safe; the safety bounds are the three Derived DECIMATION_MAX_* constants. Value: the smallest power of two strictly above 4x the largest reachable corpus model (Sphere, 4,760 faces), chosen over 65,536 because it sits below the 65,024-face thread_sweep UV sphere and therefore gives the reduced path cross-thread determinism coverage at no frozen-digest cost. Placement is deliberate and load-bearing: the threshold lives inside assess_downstream_utility, not in front of the search, so every trace below it -- and all seven frozen OD-8 census digests -- is structurally byte-identical rather than merely measured to be. Single-specimen basis (R4-shaped standing trigger): n = 1 large specimen; a second corpus model above ~4,760 faces triggers re-derivation, never silent inheritance.

registry_entries.provenance_detail: Rust-era support-pipeline execution authority with no legacy Python source and NO measurement of record. Introduced Codex-era c2b3b98; the SupportPreparationLimits::production policy that assembles it is Codex-era 73e7c13 / a8acfb9 / c2b3b98. Registered by owner ruling R5 (2026-08-05) so that no support execution cap is unregistered; registration records the inherited number and does NOT ratify it. Inherited unmeasured specialized cap on charged gate operations. Measured 2026-08-05 to be refusing an algorithm defect, not a large model: the Weeping Treant tripped it at limit+1 through a selection sort in unique_island_face_count that charged 16,795,425,332 operations where a set with identical output charges 142,646. FU-8b fixes (a), (b) and (c) landed 2026-08-06 and the treant's refusal became a stated demand, GateOperationLimit { required: 12714828544, limit: 2000000000 }. This number was then NOT raised: it became the FLOOR of the measured rule max(floor, SUPPORT_GATE_MAX_WORK_PER_BATCH_UNIT x (coverage_samples + 1) x (contacts + 1)), which leaves it the whole cap for every corpus model and admits the treant's honest linear batch. It is still the inherited unmeasured number as a floor, and it still refuses the treant's 39,223-proposal merge gate at 21,755,124,103,146 operations (FU-8c). AMENDED 2026-08-06 (FU-8d phases F2, F3 and F4): the sentence above is left standing as written and is now false twice over; this amendment states what holds instead rather than rewriting it. First, 21,755,124,103,146 has been superseded twice on that same 553,835,949-unit batch: FU-8c's GateBatchIndex took it to 201,480,535,329, FU-8d phase F2's witness-answered nearest delta took it to 7,299,316,559, and FU-8d phase F3 -- which finalizes the load partition once per batch instead of once per variant, deletes the per-variant window matrices, collapses four per-proposal planning passes into one behind a count-derived pre-check, and prices the load phase from specialized_load_resource_plan itself rather than from the gate's variants x faces model -- takes it to 9,273,857,317. That last move is a RISE over F2's figure, and it is a quadratic repriced honestly rather than a bound relaxed: the honest load term 6,592,813,742 is 1.43x the 4,618,272,984 model it replaced, while descriptor_operations falls to 136,791,451 charged once and unique_face_finalizer_work ceases to exist as a term. Second, and this is what the standing sentence gets backwards: there is NO refusal at this cap any more, at any site. Against the UNCHANGED materialization 35,445,500,736 the stated demand 9,273,857,317 is 26.2 % and exact_operations 10,457,910,996 is 29.5 %; both checks PASS, the batch is ADMITTED, and the gate EXECUTES -- 39,224 variants evaluated, a merge accepted, the next batch opened. Nothing was raised to get there: the registered value, the floor, the coefficient and the rule are all unchanged, and every figure that fell is a quadratic removed. Do NOT read any refusal figure in this entry as current; read 9,273,857,317 as a demand this cap ADMITS (single specimen, n = 1, per R4/FU-23). The treant still reaches no seal, but its stopping mode is now a WALL-CLOCK TIMEBOX rather than a typed refusal: phase F4's two clean runs at the F3 tip (PLINTH_THREADS=4, release, --features census, RSS watchdog armed at 90 GB and never fired) are EXCEEDS-TIMEBOX at 607 s and 602 s, peak RSS about 2.5 GiB, with no typed cap error in either. What consumes the timebox was sampled directly rather than inferred -- fill_proposal_nearest_delta about 61 % of main-thread samples, assess_coverage about 25 %, merged_violation_count about 4.6 %, none of it charged against this cap -- and is opened as FU-8e, which is algorithm work and not a cap to raise. Ruling R-f is therefore still NOT satisfied and SUPPORT_GATE_WORK_PER_BATCH_UNIT_OBSERVED must still NOT be re-derived: no treant run has yet COMPLETED the gate. See docs/rust-migration/support-resource-caps-2026-08-05.md sections 10 and 11 for the measurements this amendment reports. AMENDED 2026-08-07 (FU-8e phases E1-E4): every sentence above stands as written, and this amendment records that no number in it moved. FU-8e removed the merge gate's per-proposal kd-tree construction -- replaced by a one-source kNN fast path in the kernel, argued bit-identical to the tree's answer in five clauses and pinned on f64::to_bits -- and its per-variant assess_coverage, by handing a variant whose rewritten rows cannot have moved the coverage objective the batch baseline's objective. plan_proposal_nearest_delta was deliberately NOT touched, so work() is still 1 x touched_rows, the treant's touched_rows re-measured at 1,041,544,686 to the row, and the demand this cap ADMITS is still 9,273,857,317 against the same 35,445,500,736 (single specimen, n = 1, per R4/FU-23). No cap, floor, coefficient or rule was changed by E1, E2, E3 or E4. The sampled attribution quoted above is corrected on MECHANISM, not on proportion: the one-point kd-trees were free at 83.3 ns each -- all 39,223 in a batch total about 3.27 ms -- and the cost inside fill_proposal_nearest_delta was the query loop behind them, about 1.04e9 query iterations and 2.08e9 heap allocations per batch; assess_coverage's cost was two unconditional full scans of the nearest array per variant, about 254 GB of reads per batch, rather than allocation churn. Measured 2026-08-07 under ruling R-g (entire run and watchdog unsandboxed, PLINTH_THREADS=4, release, --features census, RSS watchdog armed at 90 GB and never fired): the merge round falls 63.83 s to 14.68 s (4.35x), coverage per variant 17.05 s to 0.001 s, zero coverage fallbacks across 33 rounds and about 1.29 million proposal variants, peak RSS 2.446 GiB, no typed cap error. The treant still reaches no seal and its stopping mode is still a WALL-CLOCK TIMEBOX: EXCEEDS-TIMEBOX at 601 s having completed 33 merge rounds. The tournament commits exactly one merge per round, so at most 1,365 rounds by the contact bound and about 460 at make_raking_blade's completion ratio put the post-fix gate stage at roughly 1.8 to 5.5 hours, 11x to 33x the timebox. Ruling R-f is therefore STILL NOT satisfied and SUPPORT_GATE_WORK_PER_BATCH_UNIT_OBSERVED must STILL NOT be re-derived: no treant run has yet COMPLETED the gate. The successor is opened as FU-8f -- lazy first-safe gate acceptance plus non-incremental batch preparation -- and is a RECORDED FINDING AWAITING OWNER RULING, deliberately not built, because lazy acceptance severs charged-batch from executed-batch and would re-found GateRoutePlanMismatch a second time after phase F3. ARITHMETIC CORRECTED 2026-08-07 (records fix): the kd-tree construction total in the amendment above was first written as 16.7 microseconds, which was an arithmetic slip in the design pass and not a second measurement -- 39,223 x 83.3 ns = 3.267 ms, and 16.7 microseconds across 39,223 builds would have implied 0.426 ns per construction, below one memory access. The per-build 83.3 ns is RETAINED as the design pass's measurement of record; only the product is corrected, and the conclusion it was quoted for is unchanged, because 3.27 ms is 0.009 % of the 37.33 s fill_proposal_nearest_delta frame: construction stays negligible and the fix still targets the query loop. No measured quantity, cap, floor, coefficient or rule moves. See docs/rust-migration/support-resource-caps-2026-08-05.md section 12.
